    AI Overview
    Chuck Norris (born Carlos Ray Norris in 1940, died March 2026) was an American martial artist, actor, and producer, renowned as a six-time undefeated world karate champion and a leading 1980s action star. He is best known for his role in "Walker, Texas Ranger" (1993–2001) and for launching his acting career against Bruce Lee in "The Way of the Dragon" (1972). 
    • Martial Arts Career: Norris began training in South Korea while in the Air Force, later winning the World Professional Middleweight Karate Championship in 1968. He holds an eighth-degree black belt in Tae Kwon Do and founded his own style, Chun Kuk Do.
    • Film & TV Star: He starred in films like Missing in Action, The Delta Force, and Code of Silence.
    • Personal Life & Family: Born in Ryan, Oklahoma, on March 10, 1940, he was 86 at the time of his death. He was married to Dianne Holechek (two children, Mike and Eric) and later Gena O'Kelley (twins, Dakota and Danilee).
    • Pop Culture Status: In his later years, he became an internet sensation, inspiring the humorous "Chuck Norris Facts" that highlighted his reputation for extreme strength. 
    Note: Reports indicate Chuck Norris passed away on March 20, 2026, surrounded by his family, notes Instagram.

    AI Overview
    Chuck Norris is most famous as a legendary martial artist, action film star, and for his lead role in the long-running television series Walker, Texas Ranger (1993–2001). He gained further iconic status through the internet phenomenon known as "Chuck Norris Facts," which humorously exaggerate his strength and toughness. 
    Key aspects of his fame include: 
    • Walker, Texas Ranger: His most iconic role, portraying Cordell Walker, a no-nonsense lawman.
    • Martial Arts Champion: Before Hollywood, he was a world professional middleweight karate champion and founded his own discipline, Chun Kuk Do
      .
    • Action Film Star: Known for Missing in Action, The Delta Force, and his famous fight scene with Bruce Lee in Way of the Dragon.
    • "Chuck Norris Facts": Viral Internet memes that turned him into a pop-culture icon representing ultimate strength and invincibility. 
    He is also recognized for his philanthropic work, including founding the Kickstart Kids program, and as a New York Times bestselling author.
